title: Introduction to cengenAnnotate
text: Manually annotating clusters new C. elegans single-cell dataset usually means: run Seurat::FindAllMarkers(), copy top ~20 marker genes cluster, paste CeNGEN website, visually judge whether resulting dot plot shows one cell type standing . cengenAnnotate computes judgment directly CeNGEN’s reference expression data, clusters can annotated automatically genuinely ambiguous ones come back manual review. vignette builds small synthetic reference dataset runs offline reproducibly. real use, ’ll fetch reference data CeNGEN pins board [list_cengen_datasets()] [load_cengen_reference()] instead — see last section.

title: Introduction to cengenAnnotate
text: reference long table gene, cell_type, avg_expr (unthresholded average expression) pct_expr (percent cells type expressing gene) — two quantities CeNGEN dot plot encodes color size.
code: set.seed(1) cell_types <- paste0("N", 1:6)  make_gene <- function(gene, specific_to, base = 0, high = 8, cov_high = 90, cov_low = 15) {   tibble(     gene = gene,     cell_type = cell_types,     avg_expr = ifelse(cell_types == specific_to, high, base),     pct_expr = ifelse(cell_types == specific_to, cov_high, cov_low)   ) }  reference_data <- bind_rows(   make_gene("g1", "N1"), make_gene("g2", "N1"), make_gene("g3", "N1"),   make_gene("g4", "N2"), make_gene("g5", "N2"),   make_gene("g6", "N3"), make_gene("g7", "N3"), make_gene("g8", "N3") )  reference <- new_cengen_reference(   reference_data,   meta = list(stage = "demo", sex = "demo", dataset_label = "synthetic demo reference") ) reference #> <cengen_reference> #>   stage:   demo #>   sex:     demo #>   label:   synthetic demo reference #>   prepared: ? #>   genes: 8, cell types: 6

title: Introduction to cengenAnnotate
text: prepare_marker_panel() takes raw Seurat::FindAllMarkers() output reduces top marker genes per cluster (default 20; equally weighted, fold-change used pick genes make panel).
code: markers <- tibble(   cluster = c(rep("0", 3), rep("1", 2), rep("2", 1)),   gene = c("g1", "g2", "g3", "g4", "g5", "g6"),   avg_log2FC = c(2.1, 1.8, 1.5, 1.9, 1.2, 1.0),   p_val_adj = c(0.001, 0.001, 0.001, 0.001, 0.001, 0.001) )  # cluster "0": three genes specific to N1 -> should be a clear match # cluster "1": two genes specific to N2 -> also a clear match, fewer genes # cluster "2": one gene, and we'll require at least 2 usable genes below, #   so it will be sent to review as marker-poor  prepare_marker_panel(markers, top_n = 20) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   cluster gene   rank n_requested n_used #>   <chr>   <chr> <int>       <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 0       g1        1          20      3 #> 2 0       g2        2          20      3 #> 3 0       g3        3          20      3 #> 4 1       g4        1          20      2 #> 5 1       g5        2          20      2 #> 6 2       g6        1          20      1

title: Introduction to cengenAnnotate
text: score_cengen_clusters() scores every cluster every candidate cell type classifies "annotate" need review. "annotate" clusters one cell type ’s well-covered specific across marker panel; clusters score/gap cutoffs, usable marker genes, come back "review_ambiguous" / "review_insufficient_markers" manual follow-instead. full cluster x cell-type matrix (just top 2 candidates) attached result:
code: result <- score_cengen_clusters(   markers, reference,   min_genes_used = 2 # demo data only has a few genes per cluster ) result #> # A tibble: 3 × 11 #>   cluster best_cell_type best_score second_cell_type second_score   gap #>   <chr>   <chr>               <dbl> <chr>                   <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 0       N1                  0.893 N2                      0.275 0.618 #> 2 1       N2                  0.893 N1                      0.275 0.618 #> 3 2       N3                  0.893 N1                      0.275 0.618 #> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_genes_used <int>, n_genes_requested <dbl>, #> #   n_genes_missing_from_reference <int>, n_genes_uninformative <int>, #> #   decision <chr> cengen_matrix(result) |> filter(cluster == "0") |> arrange(desc(score)) #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   cluster cell_type score n_genes_used n_genes_requested n_genes_missing_from_…¹ #>   <chr>   <chr>     <dbl>        <int>             <dbl>                   <int> #> 1 0       N1        0.893            3                 3                       0 #> 2 0       N2        0.275            3                 3                       0 #> 3 0       N3        0.275            3                 3                       0 #> 4 0       N4        0.275            3                 3                       0 #> 5 0       N5        0.275            3                 3                       0 #> 6 0       N6        0.275            3                 3                       0 #> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​n_genes_missing_from_reference #> # ℹ 1 more variable: n_genes_uninformative <int>

what: 4. Writing annotations back onto a Seurat object
title: Introduction to cengenAnnotate
text: write_cengen_annotations() explicit, opt-step — clusters sent review never silently annotated.
code: counts <- matrix(   rpois(6 * 30, lambda = 3),   nrow = 6, ncol = 30,   dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:6), paste0("cell", 1:30)) ) obj <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, min.cells = 0, min.features = 0) #> Warning: Data is of class matrix. Coercing to dgCMatrix. obj$seurat_clusters <- factor(rep(c("0", "1", "2"), each = 10))  obj <- write_cengen_annotations(obj, result) table(obj$cengen_annotation, useNA = "ifany") #>  #>   N1   N2 <NA>  #>   10   10   10

what: Automated CeNGEN-Based Annotation of Seurat Clusters
title: Automated CeNGEN-Based Annotation of Seurat Clusters
text: cengenAnnotate automates annotation Seurat clusters C. elegans single-cell data using CeNGEN reference expression data. replaces manual workflow copying marker genes CeNGEN website, reading resulting dot plot eye, judging whether cluster’s marker panel points single coherent cell type. cengenAnnotate computes “dot-plot-mirrored coherence score” every (cluster, candidate cell type) pair directly CeNGEN’s unthresholded expression data (average-expression percent-expressing values dot plot encodes color size), classifies cluster confidently annotatable need manual review, based tunable score cutoff gap next-best candidate.

title: Automated CeNGEN-Based Annotation of Seurat Clusters
text: See vignette("cengenAnnotate") complete walkthrough.
code: library(Seurat) library(cengenAnnotate)  # 1. Marker genes, as usual markers <- FindAllMarkers(seurat_obj, only.pos = TRUE)  # 2. Pick a CeNGEN reference dataset (stage/sex variant) list_cengen_datasets() reference <- load_cengen_reference("adult_herm")  # 3. Score every cluster against every candidate cell type result <- score_cengen_clusters(markers, reference) result  # 4. Write confident annotations back onto the Seurat object; ambiguous / #    marker-poor clusters are left for manual review seurat_obj <- write_cengen_annotations(seurat_obj, result)  # 5. Visually sanity-check any cluster, especially ones sent to review plot_cengen_dotplot(reference, markers, cluster = "3", scores = result)

text: score_matrix long score matrix, returned score_cengen_matrix(). cutoff Minimum best_score required auto-annotate. min_gap Minimum gap best second-best score required auto-annotate (guards ambiguous ties). min_genes_used Minimum number usable marker genes required; , cluster always sent review.

title: Classify clusters as annotatable or in need of review — classify_cengen_matches
text: tibble one row per cluster: cluster, best_cell_type, best_score, second_cell_type, second_score, gap, n_genes_used, n_genes_requested, n_genes_missing_from_reference, n_genes_uninformative, decision. Sorted best_score descending (confident cluster first), input cluster order.

title: Classify clusters as annotatable or in need of review — classify_cengen_matches
text: Decision priority, evaluated order: n_genes_used < min_genes_used: "review_insufficient_markers", regardless score (usable marker genes trust match). Else best_score >= cutoff gap >= min_gap: "annotate" (one cell type stands clearly). Otherwise: "review_ambiguous" (either candidate scores high enough, one candidate plausible).

text: cengen_scores tibble (shape scores, score matrix attribute preserved cengen_matrix() still works), decision extended include "provisional" "review_conflict", best_cell_type updated TransferData's call "provisional" rows, three new diagnostic columns: td_call, td_purity, td_mean_score.

title: Combine cengenAnnotate results with Seurat TransferData predictions — combine_with_transfer_data
text: test datasets, cengenAnnotate's "annotate" calls TransferData's confident per-cell-vote majority never disagreed. genuine conflict (methods confident, different answers) therefore treated rare edge case rather silently resolved: flagged "review_conflict", keeping cengenAnnotate's (independently validated) call best_cell_type recording TransferData's call td_call inspection. object must already Seurat::TransferData() results attached, e.g.:
code: anchors <- Seurat::FindTransferAnchors(reference = ref, query = object) predictions <- Seurat::TransferData(anchorset = anchors, refdata = ref$cell_type) object <- Seurat::AddMetaData(object, metadata = predictions)

title: Score clusters against every candidate CeNGEN cell type — score_cengen_matrix
text: gene g cell type t: cov(g,t) = 0 pct_expr(g,t) < min_pct_expr, else pct_expr(g,t) / 100. z(g,t) = (avg_expr(g,t) - mu_g) / sigma_g, mu_g/sigma_g gene g's mean/sd avg_expr across cell types. spec(g,t) = plogis(z(g,t)). s(g,t) combines two: combine = "arithmetic" (default), cov_weight * cov(g,t) + spec_weight * spec(g,t); "geometric", cov(g,t)^cov_weight * spec(g,t)^spec_weight (requires signals non-trivial simultaneously). combine = "arithmetic" default based empirical check independent ground-truth labels (see package vignette): marker panels dominated inherently sparse, low-detection gene families (e.g. many chemoreceptor genes) can near-perfect specificity (spec close 1) structurally low coverage even true cell type, since low-copy-number transcripts prone dropout. Requiring signals simultaneously high ("geometric") unfairly punishes otherwise clean, correct match. "arithmetic" lets high specificity compensate structurally-limited coverage; held-validation set roughly doubled number confidently-annotated clusters measurable loss precision (still ~100% concordant ground truth), still correctly leaving genuinely ambiguous cases (e.g. AWC_ON vs AWC_OFF) flagged review. cluster-level score cell type t mean s(g,t) cluster's usable marker genes. Genes absent reference, near-zero variance across cell types (uninformative), excluded scoring tallied diagnostic columns.
